question: why the drafter layer raises the core (ME) fault while every output is bit-exact
rtl_observation: debug-only instrumented build (debug_only_trace_patch.py, never committed to rtl/): the fault source is the ME lane BF16 multiplier ot_qwen_w12_bmul (mul=1 add=0), which fails closed (result 0, fault) when a product's biased FP32 exponent is below -6, i.e. |w*x| < 2^-133 (a subnormal that would need more than a 7-bit shift). Trace head: mf_D0_P49_trace_head.log.
cause: the seeded synthetic history (E4M3 values uniform over +-448) gives score spreads of thousands of nats, so softmax probabilities are subnormal; probability x V products fall below 2^-133. They are absorbed in the PV sums, so X/K/V stay bit-exact, but the lane contract (existing datapath, the same lanes the AR layers use) flags them. Not a DSpark program or KV-service bug.
closure: drafter layer measured at the target context with a format-valid, real-magnitude context window (the 8K prompt's target layer-0 K/V, rows < 8188, per die): k_D0r.
